entries.reason: the frame itself: named columns, a row count, a shape as a labelled pair, a row read by name or by ColumnID, and the projections. The collection conformances its columns would inherit are NOT carried, because a user-defined collection conformance does not compile with the port's Swift 6.4 at all — measured on the port's compiler at -target armv7-apple-ios6.0 and on the host's, with a fifteen-line non-generic conformance as the witness; Array, in the same standard library, conforms without trouble. The columns carry the collection's members as members instead, spelled with the labels the requirement has
entries.effect: a frame is a list of named columns keyed by name and a row count; adding a column of a name that is there replaces it, and a frame whose columns disagree on a height is invalid and says which heights rather than padding the short column
entries.source: the iOS 26.2 SDK's TabularData.swiftinterface, read for the declarations; the compilation failure measured on the port's own swiftc and on the host's; the behaviour checked by tests/backports/host/createml/tabularframe.swift, 70 checks
